ssti.idsa.exposure: Bites, water exposure, diabetic foot and surgical site infection follow separate rules; not modelled here.
ssti.idsa.necrotizing: Suspected necrotising infection: urgent surgical review; empiric broad cover spans MRSA, streptococci, Gram-negatives and anaerobes.
ssti.idsa.nonpur_severe: Severe non-purulent infection: surgical inspection plus vancomycin with a broad beta-lactam.
ssti.idsa.nonpur_mild_mrsa: Mild cellulitis with MRSA risk: an oral option that covers both streptococci and MRSA.
ssti.idsa.nonpur_mild: Mild cellulitis: an oral beta-lactam active against streptococci; 5 days, longer if not improving.
ssti.idsa.nonpur_moderate_mrsa: Moderate cellulitis with MRSA risk: a parenteral agent active against MRSA.
ssti.idsa.nonpur_moderate: Cellulitis with systemic signs: a parenteral beta-lactam active against streptococci.
ssti.idsa.pur_severe: Severe purulent infection: drainage, culture and a parenteral agent active against MRSA.
ssti.idsa.pur_moderate: Abscess with systemic signs: drainage and culture; oral MRSA cover.
ssti.idsa.pur_mild: Mild abscess: incision and drainage is enough; no antibiotic is advised.
ssti.nice.refer: Severe or necrotising infection: urgent hospital assessment.
ssti.nice.mild: Flucloxacillin first; clarithromycin, erythromycin (pregnancy) or doxycycline in penicillin allergy. 5-7 days.
ssti.nice.moderate: IV flucloxacillin when not severe; co-amoxiclav, cefuroxime, clindamycin or ceftriaxone for severe infection.
ssti.nice.facial: Near the eyes or nose: co-amoxiclav for anaerobic cover; clarithromycin plus metronidazole in allergy. Consider specialist advice.
ssti.nice.mrsa_add: Suspected or confirmed MRSA: add vancomycin or teicoplanin; linezolid only when neither can be used.
